transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. It’s nice to meet you too. I came in today because, well, I seem to be spending far too much of my day just checking on things. 

I keep opening the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes over and over again. I just have to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. And the frustrating part is... I'll do this even when I just checked them a few minutes before. It's just taking up so much of my time and I don't know why I can't stop.
When you feel the need to recheck those folders, drawers, or boxes, is it because you’re afraid something bad will happen if you don’t?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm afraid of a disaster happening, no. It's more of a nagging worry. Even when I logically know better, a thought will just keep needling me that I might have accidentally thrown away my husband's old tax papers, or maybe I put a family recipe in the wrong box. 

I just can't seem to let the thought pass. If I don't go look, I just sit there feeling like I've done something terribly careless, and the only way to get rid of that feeling is to go check again.
Do these thoughts about having misplaced or thrown something away feel intrusive and unwanted to you?

Yes, they really do. I don't want them there at all. Like I was just saying, that... that thought about my husband's tax papers or the recipe box, it just forces its way in. 

Even when I know better, it just keeps needling me. I try to push it away, but I can't seem to let it pass. It just hangs over me, making me feel like I've been terribly careless, and I just can't shake it. It's very frustrating, and definitely not something I want to be spending my time thinking about.
Do you feel that this repeated checking is excessive or unreasonable?

Yes, I certainly do. Like I mentioned when we first started talking, spending so much of my day just opening those same drawers and labeled boxes over and over... it's just too much. I know it's completely unreasonable to keep making sure my keepsakes and papers are there when I literally just checked them a few minutes before. So, yes, it is very excessive, and that's really the main reason I decided I needed to come see you.
When you check those drawers or boxes again, does doing it make the nagging feeling go away, even if only for a little while?

Yes, it does... for a little bit, anyway. The nagging feeling stops once I look and see everything is safe. 

But the relief just doesn't last. That's really why I came to see you, because I end up spending far too much of my day opening those same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes again and again. I just have to make absolutely sure the important papers and keepsakes are where I left them, even when I just checked them a few minutes before. The worry always comes right back.
Aside from checking, do you have any other repetitive rituals you feel driven to do?

No, not that I've noticed. It's really just the checking. I don't have any other habits like counting things or... or washing my hands over and over, if that's the sort of thing you mean. 

It's strictly just feeling like I need to go back and look through those drawers and boxes to make sure my things are still there. I don't feel driven to do anything else. That's really the only one.
